related_questions.question: How long do you have to be exposed to COVID before getting it?

text_blocks.snippet: The amount of time required to be exposed to COVID-19 to become infected can vary, but generally, longer exposure times increase the risk of transmission. Symptoms can appear between 2 and 14 days after exposure. While brief exposures, like fleeting contacts, pose a lower risk, prolonged interactions significantly elevate the probability of infection.

list.title: Timeframe:
list.snippet: The incubation period for COVID-19, the time between exposure and symptom onset, typically ranges from 2 to 14 days.

list.title: Duration of Exposure:
list.snippet: A study published in Nature indicated that the length of time spent near an infected individual is a major factor in determining the likelihood of transmission.

list.title: Fleeting vs. Prolonged Contacts:
list.snippet: Brief encounters of less than 30 minutes carry a much lower risk of transmission compared to extended periods of close contact.

list.title: Increased Risk:
list.snippet: As the duration of exposure increases, so does the risk of infection.
